ch-canton-1.atlas_note: Vineyards around Lake Zürich and in the Weinland north of the city. Blauburgunder (Pinot Noir) and Räuschling, an old local white grape.

ch-canton-14.atlas_note: Northern canton on the Rhine, known as Blauburgunderland for its Pinot Noir.

ch-canton-18.note: Outline follows the canton boundary. The wine areas and communal appellations inside are drawn by commune.
ch-canton-18.atlas_note: Switzerland's Pinot Noir stronghold: two thirds of the vines are Blauburgunder. The warm Föhn wind from the south, called the grape cooker, gives long ripe autumns in a valley sheltered by the Rätikon. Four villages of the Bündner Herrschaft hold about 83% of the vineyards. The law names three wine areas: the Bündner Rheintal, the Misox south of the Alps and Brusio in the Valposchiavo.
ch-canton-18.vine_area_note: 422.2 ha in the Rhine valley and Brusio plus 27.9 ha in the Misox, 2025 (BLW, Das Weinjahr 2025)
ch-canton-18.basis: Kantonale Weinverordnung BR 917.400 (in force since 1 March 2018)
ch-canton-18.grape_share_note: Share of the 422 ha in the Rhine valley and Brusio, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025 (55 varieties in all). The Misox grows mostly Merlot.

ch-canton-21.atlas_note: Italian-speaking Switzerland south of the Alps, where Merlot has been the main red grape since the early 20th century.

ch-canton-22.note: Outline follows the canton boundary. The wine areas and communal appellations inside are drawn by commune.
wineries: Cave de La Côte aux Moines
ch-canton-22.atlas_note: The second wine canton of Switzerland and the home of Chasselas. Six regional AOCs, Chablais, Lavaux, La Côte, Côtes de l'Orbe, Bonvillars and Vully, and two grand cru appellations, Dézaley and Calamin, inside Lavaux. The terraces of Lavaux are a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2007. Since 2010 the best parcels can earn the cantonal mention Premier grand cru.
ch-canton-22.grape_share_note: Chasselas about 60% of the area in 2018, down from 71% in 1994 (Statistique Vaud, Numerus 2019)
ch-canton-22.basis: Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
ch-canton-22.pgc_rule: Premier grand cru (since 2010): a named clos, château, domaine or lieu-dit approved by the cantonal commission, hand harvest, at least 6,000 vines/ha, Chasselas, Pinot Noir, Gamay, Merlot, Gamaret or Garanoir, no blending, bottled in Vaud
refs: Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2

ch-canton-23.atlas_note: Switzerland's largest wine canton, in the dry upper Rhône valley protected by the Alps. Chasselas (called Fendant here) and Pinot Noir lead, with a wealth of native varieties: Petite Arvine, Amigne, Cornalin, Humagne Rouge and Heida.

ch-canton-24.note: Outline follows the canton boundary. Vineyard plots will come from the cantonal Rebbaukataster.
ch-canton-24.atlas_note: Vineyards along Lake Neuchâtel at the foot of the Jura. Chasselas and Pinot Noir, and the pale rosé Oeil-de-Perdrix.

ch-canton-25.note: Outline follows the canton boundary. The wine areas and communal appellations inside are drawn by commune.
wineries: Domaine de La Côte d'Or Gavillet & fils
ch-canton-25.atlas_note: The first AOC of Switzerland, created in 1988, and the third wine canton. Three areas: the Rive droite or Mandement with Satigny, the largest wine commune of the country, Entre Arve et Rhône and Entre Arve et Lac. Gamay, not Chasselas, is the first grape. Half the vineyard is in 23 premiers crus, defined parcels of at least about 1 ha with lower yields.
ch-canton-25.vine_area_note: 1,246.3 ha in Switzerland and 117.4 ha in the French border zone (Viry, Challex, Saint-Julien and others), 2024. 56% red.
ch-canton-25.basis: Règlement sur la vigne et les vins, RSG M 2 50.05
ch-canton-25.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 85% of the grapes from that commune (RSG M 2 50.05 art. 58)
ch-canton-25.premiers_crus_note: 23 premiers crus with 685.8 ha, OCAN Genève 2024. Yields at most 1.0 kg/m² for Chasselas and Riesling-Sylvaner, 0.9 kg/m² for the others.
refs: Règlement sur la vigne et les vins, RSG M 2 50.05
ch-canton-25.grape_share_note: Share of the 1,363.7 ha planted, OCAN Genève 2024. Gamay 275.9 ha, Chasselas 255.6 ha, Pinot Noir 159.9 ha, Gamaret 119.2 ha, Chardonnay 117.7 ha, Merlot 53.8 ha, Garanoir 47.1 ha, Sauvignon Blanc 41.3 ha, Pinot Blanc 37.8 ha, Pinot Gris 27.5 ha.

ch-reg-gr-rheintal.basis: BR 917.400 Art. 2: one of the three wine areas of Graubünden
ch-reg-gr-rheintal.atlas_note: The Rhine valley from Fläsch on the St. Gallen border up to Bonaduz, with almost all the vines of the canton. Most of them lie on the right bank of the Rhine, on calcareous slate scree. The Bündner Herrschaft in the north is the heart of it, the Churer Rheintal around Chur the smaller rest.
ch-reg-gr-rheintal.grapes: Pinot Noir / Müller-Thurgau / Chardonnay / Pinot Blanc / Sauvignon Blanc / Pinot Gris / Completer
ch-reg-gr-rheintal.vine_area_note: Sum of the commune figures, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-rheintal.outline: Union of the communes Fläsch, Maienfeld, Jenins, Malans, Landquart, Zizers, Trimmis, Chur, Felsberg, Domat/Ems, Bonaduz. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.basis: Official production area under the 2002 ordinance (Art. 17); since 2018 the law names only the Bündner Rheintal. Labels name the village: Fläscher, Maienfelder, Jeninser, Malanser.
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.atlas_note: Four villages under the Falknis and the Rätikon, the best known Pinot Noir address of Switzerland. Pinot Noir came from Burgundy around 1630, probably with Bündner mercenaries, and Schloss Salenegg in Maienfeld has made wine since 1068. The Föhn, the warm dry wind from the south, ripens the grapes late into autumn, and the vines sit at about 500 to 650 m on calcareous slate scree. Malans keeps the Completer, a white grape first written down there in 1321.
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 235.1 of 351.8 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.producers_note: Gantenbein, Adank, Christian and Roman Hermann, Marugg and Davaz in Fläsch; Donatsch, Wegelin, Boner, Fromm, Liesch and Studach in Malans; Eichholz and Obrecht in Jenins; Schloss Salenegg in Maienfeld (Falstaff guide)
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.vine_area_note: Fläsch, Maienfeld, Jenins and Malans together, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025: about 83% of the canton
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.outline: Union of the communes Fläsch, Maienfeld, Jenins, Malans. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-flaesch.label_rule: Fläscher on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-flaesch.atlas_note: The northernmost village of Graubünden, under the Fläscherberg on the St. Gallen border. Small, with a tight group of family estates such as Gantenbein, Adank, Hermann, Marugg and Davaz.
ch-reg-gr-flaesch.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 39.0 of 65.5 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-flaesch.outline: The commune of Fläsch. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-maienfeld.label_rule: Maienfelder on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-maienfeld.atlas_note: The largest wine commune of the canton, with the most growers. Schloss Salenegg here has made wine since 1068.
ch-reg-gr-maienfeld.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 77.4 of 108.5 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-maienfeld.outline: The commune of Maienfeld. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-jenins.label_rule: Jeninser on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-jenins.atlas_note: A village high on the slope between Maienfeld and Malans. With 73% Pinot Noir it is the most red of the four Herrschaft villages.
ch-reg-gr-jenins.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 57.8 of 79.2 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-jenins.outline: The commune of Jenins. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-malans.label_rule: Malanser on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-malans.atlas_note: The village of the Completer. The grape was first written down here in 1321 and nearly died out in the 20th century; an old vine at the Completerhalde in Malans kept it alive. Its name comes from Compline, the last prayer of the day, after which the monks were allowed a glass.
ch-reg-gr-malans.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 60.9 of 98.7 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-malans.outline: The commune of Malans. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-churer-rheintal.basis: Official production area under the 2002 ordinance (Art. 17), with Igis, Zizers, Trimmis, Chur, Felsberg, Domat/Ems and Bonaduz; since 2018 part of the Bündner Rheintal
ch-reg-gr-churer-rheintal.atlas_note: The vines south of the Herrschaft, from Landquart up past Chur to Bonaduz. Zizers and Trimmis hold most of them; Chur keeps a few hectares.
ch-reg-gr-churer-rheintal.vine_area_note: Sum of the commune figures, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-churer-rheintal.outline: Union of the communes Landquart, Zizers, Trimmis, Chur, Felsberg, Domat/Ems, Bonaduz. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-zizers.label_rule: Zizerser on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-zizers.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 25.2 of 38.0 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-zizers.outline: The commune of Zizers. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-trimmis.label_rule: Trimmiser on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-trimmis.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 11.2 of 17.7 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-trimmis.outline: The commune of Trimmis. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-chur.label_rule: Churer on the label: at least 60% of the wine from the commune (BR 917.400 Art. 21)
ch-reg-gr-chur.atlas_note: The cantonal capital still has a few hectares of vines. The outline is the whole commune, which since 2021 includes Haldenstein.
ch-reg-gr-chur.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 5.8 of 7.2 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-chur.outline: The commune of Chur. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-misox.basis: BR 917.400 Art. 2 and 33 to 36: AOC Graubünden Misox or DOC Grigioni Mesolcina; or DOC Ticino under Ticino law
ch-reg-gr-misox.label_rule: AOC Graubünden Misox / DOC Mesolcina Grigioni. No commune or site names with this designation (Art. 35). Growers may instead label DOC Ticino (Art. 34).
ch-reg-gr-misox.atlas_note: The Graubünden valley south of the San Bernardino pass, Italian speaking and open to the Ticino. Here it is Merlot country, not Pinot: Ticino rules apply to grapes, yields and sugar, and Ticino runs the controls. San Vittore, at 279 m the lowest point of the canton, sits on the vineyard border with Lumino in the Ticino.
ch-reg-gr-misox.vine_area_note: BLW, Das Weinjahr 2025: 89% red. The BLW counts it with Italian-speaking Switzerland.
ch-reg-gr-misox.outline: Union of the communes Lostallo, Cama, Castaneda, Grono, Roveredo, San Vittore. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-gr-brusio.basis: BR 917.400 Art. 2: the wine area Puschlav, the commune of Brusio only
ch-reg-gr-brusio.atlas_note: A quarter of a hectare in the Valposchiavo, the smallest wine area of the canton. Much more wine is made in Poschiavo from grapes grown just over the border in the Valtellina, many of those vineyards owned by Swiss families, but that wine is Italian by origin.
ch-reg-gr-brusio.outline: The commune of Brusio. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-vd-chablais.basis: RVV art. 3 and 4: the wine communes of the Aigle district
ch-reg-vd-chablais.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 60% of the grapes from that commune; communes are named as they stood on 1 June 2009 (RVV art. 32)
ch-reg-vd-chablais.atlas_note: The upper Rhône valley between the end of Lake Geneva and the Valais. Chasselas from Yvorne, Aigle, Ollon and Bex is the classic, and the Föhn warms and dries the grapes in autumn. Villeneuve at the lake end is the gateway. In 2012 a Premier grand cru from Yvorne, L'Ovaille 1584, became the first wine of the Vaud government.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
ch-reg-vd-chablais.grape_share_note: Share of the 580.5 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Chasselas 367.1 ha, Pinot Noir 90.7 ha, Gamay 36.3 ha, Gamaret 16.9 ha, Merlot 12.2 ha.
ch-reg-vd-chablais.outline: Union of the communes Aigle, Yvorne, Corbeyrier, Ollon, Bex, Lavey-Morcles, Villeneuve (VD), Roche (VD). The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-vd-lavaux.basis: RVV art. 3 and 4: the wine communes of the Lavaux-Oron and Riviera-Pays-d'Enhaut districts and Lausanne
ch-reg-vd-lavaux.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 60% of the grapes from that commune; communes are named as they stood on 1 June 2009 (RVV art. 32)
ch-reg-vd-lavaux.atlas_note: Steep stone terraces over Lake Geneva for about 30 km from the edge of Lausanne to Chillon, built from the 11th and 12th centuries under Benedictine and Cistercian monasteries. A UNESCO World Heritage site since 2007: the listed area holds 702 ha of vines. Chasselas is two thirds of the planting.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
BAK, Lavaux vineyard terraces fact sheet
ch-reg-vd-lavaux.vine_area_note: Without the 53.9 ha of Dézaley and the 16.3 ha of Calamin, which are appellations of their own. Lausanne (0.1 ha in Lavaux) and Oron are left out of the outline.
ch-reg-vd-lavaux.grape_share_note: Share of the 734.4 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Chasselas 509.1 ha, Pinot Noir 83 ha, Gamay 33.6 ha, Gamaret 18 ha.
ch-reg-vd-lavaux.outline: Union of the communes Lutry, Pully, Paudex, Belmont-sur-Lausanne, Bourg-en-Lavaux, Puidoux, Chexbres, Rivaz, Saint-Saphorin, Chardonne, Corseaux, Corsier-sur-Vevey, Jongny, Vevey, La Tour-de-Peilz, Montreux, Veytaux, Blonay - Saint-Légier. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-vd-la-cote.basis: RVV art. 3 and 4: the wine communes of the Ouest lausannois, Morges and Nyon districts, except La Sarraz, Pompaples, Orny and Eclépens
ch-reg-vd-la-cote.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 60% of the grapes from that commune; communes are named as they stood on 1 June 2009 (RVV art. 32)
ch-reg-vd-la-cote.atlas_note: The long gentle slope between Lausanne and Geneva, facing the lake, mostly on glacial moraine. The largest region of Vaud by far. Its heart is the run of villages above Rolle, Mont-sur-Rolle, Féchy, Tartegnin, Vinzel and Luins, while Morges in the east is the largest single lieu de production of the canton.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
ch-reg-vd-la-cote.vine_area_note: About 53% of the Vaud vineyard. The outline joins the communes of its twelve lieux de production.
ch-reg-vd-la-cote.grape_share_note: Share of the 2,001.6 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Chasselas 1219.9 ha, Pinot Noir 197.2 ha, Gamay 181.1 ha, Gamaret 87.4 ha, Garanoir 67.9 ha.
ch-reg-vd-la-cote.outline: Union of the communes Aclens, Bremblens, Buchillon, Hautemorges, Chavannes-près-Renens, Chigny, Clarmont, Crissier, Denens, Denges, Echandens, Echichens, Ecublens (VD), Etoy, Gollion, Lavigny, Lonay, Lully (VD), Lussy-sur-Morges, Mex (VD), Morges, Préverenges, Prilly, Romanel-sur-Morges, Saint-Livres, Saint-Prex, Saint-Sulpice (VD), Tolochenaz, Villars-Sainte-Croix, Vaux-sur-Morges, Villars-sous-Yens, Vufflens-la-Ville, Vufflens-le-Château, Vullierens, Yens, Aubonne, Féchy, Bougy-Villars, Perroy, Allaman, Mont-sur-Rolle, Rolle, Essertines-sur-Rolle, Tartegnin, Gilly, Bursinel, Dully, Vinzel, Bursins, Luins, Begnins, Vich, Gland, Nyon, Founex, Duillier, Commugny, Crans (VD), Signy-Avenex, Arnex-sur-Nyon, Givrins, Prangins, Eysins, Coppet, Genolier, Borex, Grens, Trélex, Bogis-Bossey, Crassier, Mies, Coinsins. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-vd-cotes-orbe.basis: RVV art. 3, 4 and 10: one lieu de production
ch-reg-vd-cotes-orbe.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 60% of the grapes from that commune; communes are named as they stood on 1 June 2009 (RVV art. 32)
ch-reg-vd-cotes-orbe.atlas_note: Vines at the foot of the Jura around Orbe, north of the watershed: the water here flows to the Rhine, not the Rhône. The only region of Vaud where Gamay, not Chasselas, leads.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
ch-reg-vd-cotes-orbe.grape_share_note: Share of the 177.8 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Gamay 62.7 ha, Chasselas 29.1 ha, Pinot Noir 27.2 ha.
ch-reg-vd-cotes-orbe.outline: Union of the communes Agiez, Arnex-sur-Orbe, Baulmes, Bavois, Belmont-sur-Yverdon, Chamblon, Champvent, Chavornay, Eclépens, La Sarraz, Mathod, Montcherand, Orbe, Orny, Pompaples, Rances, Suscévaz, Valeyres-sous-Rances, Yverdon-les-Bains, Yvonand. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-vd-bonvillars.basis: RVV art. 3, 4 and 11: one lieu de production
ch-reg-vd-bonvillars.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 60% of the grapes from that commune; communes are named as they stood on 1 June 2009 (RVV art. 32). Champagne (VD) may name itself only on wine wholly from the commune, never blended.
ch-reg-vd-bonvillars.atlas_note: The north-west shore of Lake Neuchâtel below the Jura, from Grandson to Concise, the largest wine commune here. Pinot Noir is planted as much as Chasselas. The village of Champagne may put its name on the label only for wine wholly from the commune.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois, version of 1 July 2013 (art. 32)
ch-reg-vd-bonvillars.grape_share_note: Share of the 188.9 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Pinot Noir 59.1 ha, Chasselas 57.6 ha, Gamay 22.2 ha.
ch-reg-vd-bonvillars.outline: Union of the communes Bonvillars, Champagne, Concise, Corcelles-près-Concise, Fiez, Grandson, Montagny-près-Yverdon, Onnens (VD), Valeyres-sous-Montagny. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.

ch-reg-vd-vully.basis: RVV art. 3, 4 and 12, and the Fribourg wine ordinance art. 16: shared by Vully-les-Lacs (VD) and Mont-Vully (FR)
ch-reg-vd-vully.atlas_note: The Mont Vully between Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Morat, an appellation shared by Vaud and Fribourg. Vines on molasse facing the Lake of Morat, with the Fribourg villages Môtier, Praz and Lugnorre on the other side of the cantonal line.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
ch-reg-vd-vully.vine_area_note: Vaud part only. With Mont-Vully in Fribourg the appellation has about 150 ha.
ch-reg-vd-vully.grape_share_note: Share of the 56.7 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Chasselas 20.1 ha, Pinot Noir 19.5 ha.
ch-reg-vd-vully.outline: Union of the communes Vully-les-Lacs, Mont-Vully. The vines are only part of it: the vineyard layer of the map shows where they are.
wineries: Cave de La Côte aux Moines

ch-reg-vd-dezaley.basis: RVV art. 4 and 12a: AOC since 20 March 2013, every wine classed grand cru
ch-reg-vd-dezaley.label_rule: Vintage on the label, no blending, at most 10% from other Lavaux sites, higher minimum sugar. The wines may also be sold as AOC Lavaux Puidoux.
ch-reg-vd-dezaley.outline: Part of Puidoux between the Chenalettaz ravine, the Corniche road, the Forestay stream and the lake; Dézaley-Marsens is the small part north of the Corniche. Shown as a marker until the vineyard cadastre is mapped.
ch-reg-vd-dezaley.atlas_note: The steepest and most famous slope of Lavaux, slopes of over 30% falling straight to the lake between Epesses and Rivaz. Cistercian monks of the Haut-Crêt abbey cleared it in the 12th century, and the City of Lausanne has owned the Clos des Moines here since 1802. Almost all Chasselas.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2
Vaud, AOC pour le Dézaley et le Calamin (2013)
City of Lausanne, Clos des Moines
ch-reg-vd-dezaley.vine_area_note: 49.9 ha of Dézaley and 3.9 ha of Dézaley-Marsens, 2019
ch-reg-vd-dezaley.grape_share_note: Share of the 53.9 ha planted, Registre cantonal des vignes VD, 2019. Chasselas 46.3 ha, Merlot 2.1 ha, Gamay 1.8 ha, Pinot Noir 1.7 ha.

ch-reg-vd-calamin.basis: RVV art. 4 and 12b: AOC since 20 March 2013, every wine classed grand cru
ch-reg-vd-calamin.label_rule: Vintage on the label, no blending, at most 10% from other Lavaux sites, higher minimum sugar. The wines may also be sold as AOC Lavaux Epesses.
ch-reg-vd-calamin.outline: The part of the former commune of Epesses south of the Corniche road. Drawn from OpenStreetMap, where the vineyard is mapped as AOC Calamin Grand cru: 15.0 ha on the map against 16.3 ha registered.
ch-reg-vd-calamin.atlas_note: The smallest appellation of Vaud, a single slope below the village of Epesses between Cully and Dézaley. Practically all Chasselas.
refs: Vaud, Registre cantonal des vignes, 1 Nov 2019
